conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Good morning. I'm Dr. Lee, one of your care team doctors. You're here for a planned surgery to remove a mass in your left temporal lobe. How are you feeling today?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Morning, Doctor. I’m a bit nervous, but okay. The headaches are still there—pressure at the back of my head.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: I understand. The MRI before surgery showed the mass has grown, which is why we’re moving forward with the resection. We’ll monitor you closely after.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: And my speech? I’ve been having trouble finding words since the last visit.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: That could be related to the mass. After surgery, we’ll watch for any changes. Speech therapy will be involved if needed.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Hi, we’ve just finished the craniotomy. The surgery went well. We removed the mass safely.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: That’s good… I feel foggy. Can’t… find the right words.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’re experiencing expressive aphasia—difficulty speaking. It’s common after this type of surgery. A CT scan shows no bleeding. We’ll keep monitoring you in the ICU.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’ve noticed your sodium is low—125. It’s likely due to SIADH, possibly worsened by your blood pressure medication.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I have diabetes insipidus too. Could that be involved?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, exactly. We’ve paused your DDAVP for now because of the low sodium. We’re giving salt tablets and stopping hydrochlorothiazide. We’ll restart DDAVP once your sodium stabilizes.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Your sodium is improving—127 now. We’re restarting DDAVP at a lower dose. Endocrine is helping us balance this.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Good. And the mass—any idea what it is?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Preliminary pathology suggests high-grade B-cell lymphoma. But we need to check if it’s only in the brain or elsewhere.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Lymphoma? But I’ve had those enlarged lymph nodes for years.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, from your histiocytosis. But we need to be sure the lymphoma hasn’t spread. We’ll do a lymph node biopsy and bone marrow test.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Your aphasia is improving. Speech therapy will start today to help with word-finding.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: That’s a relief. I was worried I’d never speak normally again.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Most patients recover well. We’re also watching your hepatitis B. Your viral load is undetectable, so no treatment is needed now.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You had chest pain yesterday when we flushed your line?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Yes, sharp pain in my right chest. Still a bit tender.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: The CT didn’t show a clot or pneumonia. Troponin was normal. Likely musculoskeletal from the line. We’ll keep an eye on it.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Your CK was elevated after surgery but is now normal. That explains the muscle soreness.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Good. And the lymph node biopsy—when will we know?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: It’s scheduled for tomorrow. We’ll target a node in your groin. Early looks suggest it’s not aggressive like the brain lesion.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’re about to do the lymph node biopsy. It’s ultrasound-guided and should take about 30 minutes.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Will it hurt?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’ll numb the area. You might feel pressure, but not sharp pain. We’ll get both aspirate and a small core sample.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Biopsy went well. Sample sent to pathology. We’ll do the bone marrow biopsy tomorrow.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Any word on EBV? I read it’s linked to lymphoma.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Your EBV tests show past infection—VCA IgG and EBNA positive, IgM negative. That’s common and not active disease.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Time for the bone marrow biopsy. It’ll be from your hip. We’ll use local anesthetic.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: After my hip replacement? Will it be okay?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’ll use the opposite side. You should be fine. It’ll help us stage the lymphoma.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Biopsy complete. Minimal discomfort reported. Pathology pending.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Today we start chemotherapy—high-dose methotrexate. It’s strong, so we’ll give IV fluids, sodium bicarbonate, and monitor your levels.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Will I lose my hair? Feel sick?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Hair loss is possible. We’ll give anti-nausea meds. Leucovorin rescue starts tomorrow to protect your cells.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Chemo infusion is complete. You tolerated it well. We’ll check methotrexate levels every 24 hours.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I feel okay so far. Tired, but no nausea.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Your methotrexate level is dropping well. Leucovorin is helping clear it. Your aphasia continues to improve.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: That’s great. Can I go home soon?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, likely tomorrow. We’ll send you home with leucovorin and sodium bicarbonate for one more day to finish clearing the chemo.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Your labs are stable. Sodium is 127, normal for you now. DDAVP is well-titrated.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: And the seizures? I’m still on Keppra.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, continue levetiracetam twice daily. It’s controlling your symptoms well.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’re adding famotidine to protect your stomach from dexamethasone. And clonazepam for anxiety and sleep.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I’ve been anxious. Thanks for that.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Good news—you’re cleared to go home. We’ll remove your central line.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: What about the lymph node and marrow results?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Preliminary review shows lymphocytes but not aggressive like the brain tumor. Final results pending, but it looks like the lymphoma is confined to the CNS.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: So just brain lymphoma?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes. That means treatment can focus on the brain. You’ll continue with more chemo cycles as an outpatient.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: And my wife can help check the incision?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, daily. Watch for redness, swelling, or drainage. Call if fever hits 101 or higher.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: No lifting, right?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Nothing over 10 pounds. Walk as you feel able. Speech therapy will continue at home.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: And my meds—dexamethasone, leucovorin, sodium bicarb for one day?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Exactly. Take them as prescribed. Stop hydrochlorothiazide. Continue lisinopril, DDAVP, and levetiracetam.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Thank you, Doctor. I feel ready to go home.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’ve done well. We’ll see you in follow-up. Rest, stay hydrated, and call with any concerns.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I will. Thanks for everything.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Take care. Safe travels home.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: One last thing—can I drink coffee?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, but avoid carbonated drinks and vitamin C with meals—they can interfere with methotrexate clearance.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Got it. No soda, no orange juice with meals.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Exactly. You’re all set.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Appreciate it.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’ll schedule your next chemo cycle soon. Rest up.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Will do.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: And keep using the incentive spirometer at home—five times an hour while awake.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I’ll keep it by my chair.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Perfect. You’re ready to be discharged.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Thanks again.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Take care. We’ll see you soon.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Bye.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Goodbye.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: One more—can I drive?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Not yet. Wait for clearance at your follow-up. Use rideshare or family for now.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Understood.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: All set. Discharge papers are ready.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Thank you.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Take care. We’re here if you need us.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I appreciate that.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’re welcome. Have a safe trip home.
